messages:
Sam W: Heads-up: seeing spike in tail latency on gpu-rack27. NVLink link_down counters are flashing on rack27-gpu02..gpu06, Xid 13s and repeated AER messages in dmesg. Notified because several inference pods hit 95th p99.
infra-bot: [ALERT] nvlink.link_down rate > 20/min on cluster=gpu-prod, rack=rack27 (auto-detected) :warning:
Maria L: on it. Can you paste a short dmesg snippet and nvidia-smi output? also which model routes hit the p99?
Sam W: quick dmesg snippet:
```
[317892.123456] pcieport 0000:65:00.0: PCIe AER: Corrected error received: 00000040
[317892.123460] NVRM: Xid (13) at 0x0000000000000000
[317893.000100] nvlink0: link_down event on GPU 00000000:65:00.0
```
nvidia-smi topo output shows broken NVLink topology for gpu05 (no links reported).
Maria L: Ok — sounds like transient link flaps. Jordan, can you grab ECC/Xid counters and kernel PCIe AER stats across affected nodes?
Jordan P: running quick scrape:
```
gpu-scrape --nodes rack27-gpu02,rack27-gpu03,rack27-gpu04,rack27-gpu05,rack27-gpu06 --metrics nvlink_errors,ecc_corrected,xid --out /tmp/rack27-flap.json
```
sample returned: gpu05 nvlink_errors=42 xid13=7 ecc_corr=3
Jordan P: seeing concentrated errors on gpu05 and gpu03. Others have low counts.
Kevin R: If gpu05 is the worst, we should drain it and repro in maintenance. Propose drain order: gpu05 -> gpu03 -> others if still noisy. No full rack drain yet.
Maria L: Agreed. Quick mitigation: move heavy low-latency routes off rack27 for next 30m (route policy changed) and start draining gpu05.
Sam W: done: `rb-drain --node rack27-gpu05 --reason "nvlink link flaps / Xid 13"` :white_check_mark:
Maria L: While draining, collect persistent logs: `journalctl -k -u nvidia* --since "-1h" > /tmp/gpu05-kernel.log` and `dmesg -T > /tmp/gpu05-dmesg.log`. Also capture pci config space: `setpci -s 65:00.0 CAP_EXP+4.L` (just in case).
Jordan P: I restarted the nvidia driver on gpu05 (soft restart) to see if flaps stop: `systemctl restart nvidia-persistenced` — flaps paused for ~2min, then returned.
Maria L: That suggests hardware-level instability, not just driver. Next step: schedule scheduled-cold-reboot (power cycle) for gpu05 during maintenance window in 20m. If flaps persist after power cycle, escalate to RMA.
Kevin R: Vendor RMA path: log a case with component trace + error counts + reproduction steps. If nvlink lanes show physical degradation, RMA likely.
Sam W: Impact note: small drop in p99 for text-generation routes (model-3b) seen while gpu05 was noisy. Migration helped.
Maria L: Triage notes added to incident board. Action items:
- Jordan: upload /tmp/rack27-flap.json and logs to S3 (s3://redwood/debug/rack27/1876543210)
- Kevin: coordinate maintenance window and RMA ticket if needed
- Sam: keep routing rule in place until gpu05 healthy
If power-cycle fixes it, we'll monitor 24h and then decide on permanent swap.
Jordan P: uploaded logs: s3://redwood/debug/rack27/1876543210/logs.tar.gz :thumbsup:
infra-bot: [INFO] node rack27-gpu05 drained by Sam W at 1876543285
Maria L: follow-up: if we see Xid 31 or uncorrectable ECC counts rising after reboot, treat as immediate RMA. For now tracking as "intermittent link flicker". :eyes:
Kevin R: I'll prep RMA packet template with serial + error summary. Tagging @hardware-support for next steps.
Sam W: thanks team — I'll keep a watch on p99 and update thread. :shipit:
